title: 1954 AHSME Problem 30
statement: \(A\) and \(B\) together can do a job in \(2\) days; \(B\) and \(C\) can do it in four days; and \(A\) and \(C\) in \(2\dfrac25\) days. The number of days required for \(A\) to do the job alone is:

solutions.text:
Let \(a,b,c\) be the individual daily rates. Then \[ \begin{aligned} a+b&=\frac12,\\ b+c&=\frac14,\\ a+c&=\frac5{12}. \end{aligned} \] Thus \[ \begin{aligned} 2a&=(a+b)+(a+c)\\ &\quad{}-(b+c)\\ &=\frac12+\frac5{12}-\frac14\\ &=\frac23, \end{aligned} \] so \(a=\frac{1}{3}.\) Therefore \(A\) needs \(3\) days.

Thus, the correct answer is B.
hints: Let \(a,b,c\) be the fractions of the job completed per day
